svg.font-family: Inter, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Storefront schema — order to fulfilment
svg.desc: A crow's-foot (Information Engineering) entity-relationship diagram of a storefront database. Nine tables sit on a three-by-three grid with ORDER as the hub in the middle: CUSTOMER, PAYMENT and SHIPMENT across the top, ADDRESS, ORDER and ORDER_LINE across the middle, CATEGORY, PRODUCT and INVENTORY across the bottom. Each table is a white box outlined in dark slate, with the table name centred in a header band above a rule and one row per column beneath, showing the column name on the left and its data type on the right; primary-key column names are underlined and carry a solid blue PK tag, foreign keys a solid amber FK tag. Ten relationship lines run between the boxes at right angles, each labelled with the verb that describes it and ending in crow's-foot symbols that state how many rows may take part: a bar for exactly one, a circle for zero or one, a three-tine foot for many. ORDER_LINE resolves the many-to-many between ORDER and PRODUCT, and CATEGORY loops back on itself for parent categories. A legend at the bottom right explains the four cardinality symbols.
